quality_assessment: Excellent chapter with comprehensive coverage of encoding features. Only minor enhancements needed for completeness.

issues.description: Chapter mentions WHATWG standard but doesn't explicitly state that encoding_rs crate provides the implementation
issues.should_add: Mention that ripgrep uses the encoding_rs crate (via encoding_rs_io) to implement WHATWG encoding standard support
issues.fix_suggestion: Add a note in the 'Supported Encodings' section: 'ripgrep uses the encoding_rs crate, which provides a complete implementation of the WHATWG Encoding Standard.'

issues.description: Chapter states 'BOM overrides explicit encoding' but could use a concrete example showing this behavior
issues.current_content: **BOM overrides explicit encoding:** Even if you specify `--encoding=latin1`, a file with a UTF-16 BOM will be treated as UTF-16.
issues.should_be: Add a concrete example showing the override behavior with sample output
issues.fix_suggestion:
Add an example after line 107:
```bash
# Even though we specify latin1, the UTF-16 BOM is detected and used instead
rg -E latin1 'pattern' utf16-file-with-bom
# ripgrep uses UTF-16 (from BOM) not latin1
```

issues.description: Chapter doesn't specify that only UTF-8, UTF-16LE, and UTF-16BE BOMs are detected, not all possible BOMs
issues.should_add: Clarify that BOM detection is limited to these three encodings specifically
issues.fix_suggestion: Enhance the BOM Sniffing section around line 92-96 to state: 'ripgrep detects BOMs for UTF-8, UTF-16 Little Endian, and UTF-16 Big Endian only. Other encodings in the WHATWG standard that have BOMs are not automatically detected and require explicit --encoding specification.'

issues.description: Chapter doesn't mention using --debug flag to understand encoding detection decisions
issues.should_add: Recommend using --debug to see what encoding ripgrep detected/used
issues.fix_suggestion: Add to the troubleshooting section (around line 286): 'Use --debug flag to see encoding detection: `rg --debug pattern file` will show which encoding was detected via BOM or what transcoding is being performed.'
issues.source_reference: crates/core/flags/defs.rs (--debug flag exists and shows encoding info)

issues.description: Section explains the assumption well but could clarify why it matters for performance
issues.current_content: **By default, ripgrep assumes files are ASCII-compatible.** This is a critical assumption that affects how searches work.
issues.should_be: Explain the performance benefit: avoiding transcoding overhead for ASCII-compatible files
issues.fix_suggestion: Add after line 138: 'This assumption is a performance optimization: ASCII-compatible files can be searched directly without transcoding overhead, making searches significantly faster than if every file required transcoding to UTF-8.'
issues.source_reference: crates/searcher/src/searcher/mod.rs:529-532 (when no BOM found, search as-is for performance)

positive_aspects: Comprehensive coverage of all three encoding modes (Auto, Explicit, Disabled)
Excellent explanation of BOM sniffing mechanism and byte sequences
Clear documentation of --encoding flag with multiple examples
Good coverage of transcoding behavior and invalid byte handling
Helpful troubleshooting section with practical solutions
Accurate description of ASCII compatibility assumption and its implications
Good practical examples covering common use cases (UTF-16, GBK, Cyrillic, etc.)
Clear explanation of interaction with Unicode regex features
Performance considerations section is helpful and accurate
improvement_suggestions: Add a mention of encoding_rs crate in the Supported Encodings section for transparency
Include a concrete example showing BOM override behavior
Clarify that only UTF-8/UTF-16LE/UTF-16BE BOMs are auto-detected
Add --debug flag recommendation to troubleshooting for encoding issues
Explain the performance benefit of the ASCII compatibility assumption
Consider adding a decision tree diagram: 'When does ripgrep transcode?' showing BOM detection -> explicit encoding -> pass-through flow
Could add a note about how to verify file encoding before searching (using file command or hexdump)
Consider mentioning common encoding detection mistakes (e.g., assuming UTF-8 when file is actually latin1)

metadata.validation_focus: Verify encoding behavior and --encoding flag documentation is complete
